additions.reason: The teaching re-reads the verse 'וְגַם נֵצַח יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא יְשַׁקֵּר' such that 'נֵצַח יִשְׂרָאֵל' = the Eternal One of Israel (God's attribute of nitzachon) and 'לֹא יְשַׁקֵּר' = does not lie = IS truth. The statement 'הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אַף בְּהַנִּצָּחוֹן הוּא אֱמֶת, וְאֵינוֹ מְשַׁקֵּר' ('God even in nitzachon is truth and does not lie') has the semantic structure of a bechina equation: it identifies divine nitzachon with truth not as a causal sequence (nitzachon produces truth) but as an ontological identity (they are the same attribute in God). The formal בְּחִינַת keyword is absent, but the identification structure is present: 'הוּא אֱמֶת' — 'it IS truth.' The verse re-reading at the end ('וְזֶהוּ: וְגַם נֵצַח יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא יְשַׁקֵּר') confirms this is an ontological claim about God's nature, not a causal chain. This is the primary bechina pair of the Torah.
additions.source_quote: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אַף בְּהַנִּצָּחוֹן הוּא אֱמֶת, וְאֵינוֹ מְשַׁקֵּר, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם. וְזֶהוּ: וְגַם נֵצַח יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא יְשַׁקֵּר
additions.classification_note: This proposed edge uses 'הוּא אֱמֶת' (= 'is truth') as the bechina marker. While this does not employ the canonical 'הוּא בְּחִינַת Y' formula, the statement 'in God's nitzachon He is truth' is structurally identical to a bechina equation: it equates two aspects of the same divine attribute. The alternative classification would be eitza ('nitzachon produces truthfulness'), but the text does not describe a sequence of production — it states an identity ('הוּא אֱמֶת' not 'מוֹצִיא אֱמֶת'). Classification as bechina is correct.

proposed_edge.proof: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אַף בְּהַנִּצָּחוֹן הוּא אֱמֶת, וְאֵינוֹ מְשַׁקֵּר — וְזֶהוּ: וְגַם נֵצַח יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא יְשַׁקֵּר

additions.reason: The teaching states: 'מִדַּת הַנִּצָּחוֹן אֵינָהּ סוֹבֶלֶת הָאֱמֶת, כִּי אַף אִם יֵרָאֶה לָעֵינַיִם דְּבַר אֱמֶת, יִדְחֶה אוֹתוֹ מֵחֲמַת הַנִּצָּחוֹן, וְזֶה מְבֹרָר מְאֹד.' This is the negative pole of the teaching. The relationship between מִדַּת הַנִּצָּחוֹן and the rejection of truth is presented in the text as causal/behavioral: the nitzachon attribute CAUSES one to reject truth. Strictly speaking, this sounds like an eitza formulation. However, the deeper claim is ontological: the quality of human contentiousness IS, at its essence, the quality of truth-rejection. A person in the grip of nitzachon does not merely reject truth occasionally — the attribute itself IS incompatible with truth. 'אֵינָהּ סוֹבֶלֶת' (does not tolerate) describes an essential, structural incompatibility, not merely a frequent consequence. This structural incompatibility — human nitzachon = truth-rejection by definition — is the bechina identification. The polarity is 'evil' because this is the attribute that distances one from God, Who is truth.
additions.source_quote: מִדַּת הַנִּצָּחוֹן אֵינָהּ סוֹבֶלֶת הָאֱמֶת, כִּי אַף אִם יֵרָאֶה לָעֵינַיִם דְּבַר אֱמֶת, יִדְחֶה אוֹתוֹ מֵחֲמַת הַנִּצָּחוֹן, וְזֶה מְבֹרָר מְאֹד
additions.classification_note: This proposed edge sits on the boundary between bechina and eitza. The surface reading ('nitzachon causes one to reject truth') is eitza-like. However, the teaching's claim is stronger: the nitzachon-attribute and truth-rejection are the same thing — they are two descriptions of the same essential nature. 'אֵינָהּ סוֹבֶלֶת הָאֱמֶת' (does not tolerate truth) is not just 'produces rejection of truth' — it says that tolerance of truth is incompatible with nitzachon's essence. This is an ontological incompatibility, not a causal sequence. Classification as bechina (shared nature: both describe the same failing in human character) is justified. An alternative eitza coding would lose the structural-identity claim. Note: if the dataset team prefers eitza for this edge, it would not materially affect the package map since the two nodes would still be associated with the same conceptual domain in this Torah.

The phrase 'הוּא אֱמֶת' (is truth) is the closest this Torah comes to explicit bechina language — 'X IS Y' without the intermediate bechina-marker. The comparison structure ('not like flesh-and-blood — but God...') is the rhetorical frame for the positive bechina claim.
bechina_language_scan.line_4: 'וְזֶהוּ: וְגַם נֵצַח יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא יְשַׁקֵּר.' Return to the verse as the proof text for the positive bechina claim established in line 3. The word 'וְזֶהוּ' (and this is [the meaning of]) is a standard Rebbe Nachman formula for identifying a verse with the conceptual equation just stated — functionally equivalent to 'the verse proves/states the bechina.' Using שֶׁקֶר as a node would add a concept not present by name in the text. The source's language focuses on the rejection of truth rather than on falsehood as an active force. Excluded in favor of דְּחִיַּת הָאֱמֶת.

structural_observations: Torah #122 is one of the most compressed Torahs in Likutay Moharan — 4 lines, one verse, one contrast, one re-reading of the verse. It is purely aphoristic.

The entire teaching is structured around the bifurcation of the word נֵצַח into its two senses: (1) contentiousness/victory (human quality) and (2) the Eternal One of Israel (divine name/attribute). This double-meaning is the hermeneutic key.

The teaching does not use formal בְּחִינַת language anywhere. This is unusual for Rebbe Nachman but consistent with the aphoristic genre: the equation is stated directly ('הוּא אֱמֶת') rather than through the formal identification formula.
The two proposed edges (נֵצַח יִשְׂרָאֵל ↔ אֱמֶת; מִדַּת הַנִּצָּחוֹן ↔ דְּחִיַּת הָאֱמֶת) together capture the Torah's binary structure completely. No third concept-pair exists in the text.

The good/evil mirror is maximally direct: the same word (נִצָּחוֹן/נֵצַח) generates both the good package (God's eternal truthfulness) and the evil package (human contentiousness that rejects truth). This is the mirror operating at the level of the single word's polysemy.

There are no eitza edges to propose for Torah #122. The teaching is not structured as cause-and-effect; it is an aphoristic contrast. No practical instruction is given, and no chain of consequences is described.
